facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s with systemic sclerosis presented with a pruritic rash that had been present for 3 months
The patient denied any known preceding triggers or trauma to the area of the rash
He had tried treating with topical aloe, without improvement
Review of systems was negative for any new or worsening constitutional, respiratory, or gastrointestinal symptoms
Past medical history included heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon
He was receiving mycophenolate mofetil, 1 g twice daily
Examination findings were notable for firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk
There was no appreciable skin tightening in the affected areas
Complete blood cell count with differential was unremarkable

Lesional punch biopsy specimens showed nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles, with one additionally showing homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles in haphazard array
Tissue cultures obtained by punch biopsy were negative for bacteria, fungus, and acid-fast bacillus
Firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a pruritic rash, firm red-brown plaques, and nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers is consistent with NSF, a condition associated with systemic sclerosis and renal disease.
The patient's past medical history of systemic sclerosis, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon, along with the presence of firm red-brown plaques, supports a diagnosis of scleroderma.

The patient's presentation with firm red-brown plaques, nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers, and absence of skin tightening is consistent with morphea, a condition characterized by localized scleroderma.

The patient's presentation with a pruritic rash, firm red-brown plaques, and homogeneous, brightly eosinophilic collagen bundles is consistent with EF, a condition characterized by inflammation and fibrosis of the fascia.

rationales.F01: The presence of a pruritic rash in a patient with systemic sclerosis suggests a possible connection to scleroderma.
rationales.F05: The patient's past medical history of heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon is highly suggestive of scleroderma.
rationales.F07: The presence of firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk is consistent with morphea and eosinophilic fasciitis.
rationales.F08: The absence of appreciable skin tightening in the affected areas makes scleroderma less likely.
rationales.F10: The lesional punch biopsy specimens showing nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles is highly suggestive of scleroderma, morphea, and eosinophilic fasciitis.
rationales.F11: The negative tissue cultures make nephrogenic systemic fibrosis less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: Morphea best explains the firm, red-brown plaques without skin tightening and the biopsy findings of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers, with no appreciable skin tightening in the affected areas.
